extracted.intended_audience: general CNN readers interested in Japan, mental health, and media controversies
extracted.subtask_description: A journalistic news article describing the Aokigahara 'suicide forest', the Logan Paul video controversy, cultural context, statistics, expert commentary, survivor accounts, and prevention efforts. Aimed at informing the public about the issue and its wider social implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid trivializing or monetizing suicide content
rubrics_metrics.description: The article highlights outrage that a foreigner would 'trivialize or monetize it through YouTube' and notes Paul denied monetizing the clip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat suicide as clickbait or monetize footage of apparent suicide victims; if such content is published, acknowledge harm, provide apologies where appropriate, and avoid sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contextual statistics and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: The story supplies national suicide figures and age-adjusted rates (e.g., 'Japan was ranked 26th globally... 15.4 suicides per 100,000 population') and compares Japan to other developed nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include authoritative statistical context (WHO, national ministries) and peer-country comparisons to help readers understand scale and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include expert commentary and research citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The article quotes experts (e.g., Karen Nakamura; Emory anthropologist Chikako Ozawa-de Silva; psychiatrist Dr. Yoshitomo Takahashi) and references research and government reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant scholars, clinicians, and official reports to explain cultural, social, and clinical aspects; use expert views to interpret data and motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: List and publicize crisis resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece includes 'Resources for help' with hotline numbers (National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, Trevor Lifeline, Trans Lifeline, Crisis Text Line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on suicide, provide clear, localizable crisis contacts (phone numbers, text codes) so readers in distress can access help immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on local prevention measures (security cameras)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local authorities 'posted security cameras at the entrances of the forest, hoping to track those who walk inside.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concrete prevention steps taken by authorities, including surveillance and how they're intended to work, to inform readers about interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on local prevention measures (raise bridge rails)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local government mentions 'raising the height of bridge rails' as a prevention method in the forest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include physical-environment interventions and their rationale when covering sites with frequent suicides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on local prevention measures (train volunteers)
rubrics_metrics.description: One prevention method is 'training volunteers to talk to potentially suicidal visitors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note community-based interventions like volunteer training and explain their intended role in prevention and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on local prevention measures (increase police patrolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities considered 'increasing police patrolling at the entrances of the forest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include law-enforcement or patrol-based strategies and any discussion of effectiveness or community concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage media that may promote suicidal sites
rubrics_metrics.description: The local government mentions 'discouraging movies and TV shows that might promote the forest's reputation as a place to end one's life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how media portrayals can affect site reputation and suicide contagion; recommend caution in dramatizations and avoid glamorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore motives and social dynamics behind site selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts suggest reasons people come to Aokigahara: belief they 'would be able to die successfully without being noticed,' desire 'to die with others,' and online forums offering social connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate psychological, social, and media-related motives for choosing specific suicide sites, using survivor interviews and academic research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report socioeconomic and demographic risk factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The article lists risk factors cited by studies and government materials: 'academic pressures, depression, overwork, financial struggles and unemployment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize suicide within broader socioeconomic trends (economic recession, employment) and demographic patterns (gender differences in rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain cultural attitudes and language about suicide
rubrics_metrics.description: The story explains cultural framing such as the Japanese term 'jiketsu' ('to decide for yourself') and notes stigma around receiving mental health care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how cultural meanings, religious views, and stigma influence both prevalence and help-seeking; advise culturally informed clinical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use survivor interviews to illuminate lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The article includes an interview with a man who attempted suicide in Aokigahara describing his motives and experience ('My will to live disappeared...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include first-person survivor accounts to humanize issues, while treating them sensitively and protecting identities as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical and cultural background on site
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece references cultural works linking Aokigahara to suicide (a 1960 novel by Seicho Matsumoto, the 2016 film 'The Forest') and notes the site's long-standing reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give historical and cultural context (literature, film, folklore) that has shaped public perceptions of the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue clarifications and updates when reporting details change
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Clarification' notes the story was updated to reflect that 'Logan Paul said he did not monetize the controversial YouTube video.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparency: correct or clarify factual inaccuracies promptly and annotate articles with updates so readers see changes to the record.
